_meta.note: Wearable data SOURCES and the unification/merge policy. Each source has an ingestion mode, schema-stability posture, unit convention, trust tier (D22), and known quirks. The merge policy resolves the same metric arriving from several sources into one canonical series. The robustness section is the contract that lets the pipeline absorb upstream changes from Terra / HealthKit / vendor clouds without corrupting baselines. Illustrative; re-verify (README §5.6).

terra.label: Terra (aggregator API)
terra.units: documented per resource; mixed SI/imperial by provider
terra.schema: versioned; additive fields common; provider gaps when device disconnected
terra.role: primary unifier — already normalises many providers, but DOES pass through provider-specific units, sampling, and algorithm differences
quirks: webhook can deliver out-of-order / late (re-sync) payloads
a single user may have multiple connected providers → duplicate metrics
deauth / token-expiry silently stops the feed (looks like a gap)

healthkit.label: Apple HealthKit (on-device, iOS)
healthkit.trust: device-dependent (Watch ECG/SpO₂ higher; phone steps lower)
healthkit.ingest: on-device query / observer; app must be foregrounded or have background delivery; data leaves device only via our app
healthkit.units: HKUnit per type; SpO₂ as FRACTION, HRV as SDNN, temp ABSOLUTE
healthkit.schema: stable type identifiers; new types per iOS release; locale-dependent units (mph/mi in US)
quirks: multiple source apps write the same type → overlap/duplication
user can revoke per-type permission at any time → partial gaps
deleted samples leave holes; HKDeletedObject must be honoured
time zone stored per sample (HKMetadataKeyTimeZone) — not always present

healthconnect.label: Google Health Connect (Android)
healthconnect.ingest: on-device read with permission; change-tokens for incremental sync
healthconnect.schema: record types versioned; data-origin (package) per record

device_clouds.label: Vendor cloud APIs (Oura, Whoop, Garmin, Fitbit, Withings, Polar, Dexcom, Libre)
device_clouds.ingest: OAuth + webhook or polling per vendor
device_clouds.units: vendor-specific (Fitbit AZM, Whoop strain, Oura readiness) — many are PROPRIETARY composite scores
quirks: proprietary scores (readiness/recovery/strain) are NOT comparable across vendors — recompute from raw where possible
Fitbit reports VO₂max as a range/score, not a point

order: 1. TRUST TIER — clinical-grade (CGM, cuff, ECG, HSAT) > consumer-validated (Watch/Oura/Whoop) > inferential (sleep stages, VO₂max est.)
2. NATIVE RESOLUTION — within a tier, prefer the higher native sampling rate / finer granularity
3. RECENCY — prefer the freshest non-stale sample; older confirmations raise confidence, conflicts lower it
4. DE-DUPLICATE — collapse overlapping time intervals (steps, sleep) to a single source per interval before aggregating
5. NEVER POOL non-comparable definitions (SDNN≠RMSSD, absolute≠deviation, vendor scores) — keep separate series, choose one canonical
merge_policy.conflict: When two trusted sources disagree beyond a metric-specific tolerance, take the higher-trust source, FLAG the conflict, and lower Confidence; never silently average across incompatible definitions.
merge_policy.single_source_per_interval: For additive/count metrics (steps, active minutes, sleep intervals) pick ONE source per time interval to avoid double-counting; for point metrics (resting HR, VO₂max) pick one source per day.

robustness.contract: The ingest layer must absorb upstream change WITHOUT corrupting baselines. Guarantees:
rules: SCHEMA TOLERANCE — unknown/new fields are ignored, never fatal; missing expected fields degrade gracefully to 'absent', not error.
VERSION PINNING — record the source schema version with every sample; a version change triggers a re-validation pass, not silent ingestion.
VALIDATION GATE — every inbound sample passes type/unit/plausibility validation (see baseline-dq-rules.json) BEFORE it can touch a baseline; rejects are quarantined + logged, not dropped silently.
UNIT GUARD — a sample whose unit can't be resolved to the canonical unit is quarantined (never assumed).
IDEMPOTENT INGEST — every sample carries a stable source id; re-delivered/duplicate payloads are no-ops (handles webhook replays + backfill).
CANARY/RECOMPUTE — baselines are recomputable from the immutable raw store; a discovered upstream bug is fixed by reprocessing, not patching baselines in place.
PROVENANCE — every baseline keeps the source, device, unit, schema-version and transform of each contributing sample, so any corruption is traceable and reversible.
